Article Title: Game of one-upmanship? For fourth day in a row, INDIA bloc MPs hit the streets ahead of CJP's Jantar Mantar 2.0
Article Text:
With another CJP buildup in the making, the opposition parties perhaps don’t want to be 'missing in action' this time around

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: For four days in a row, opposition leaders have hit the streets of the national capital, demanding removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls. On September 30, when the INDIA bloc announced its 6-point protest plan against the CEC, it mentioned one street protest in the national capital - a march by all its MPs to the EC office on October 6.But the script changed.The opposition MPs, led by the Congress, returned to the streets with a march to Jantar Mantar on October 7, to Rajghat on October 8 and to Rashtrapati Bhawan on October 9. The police went all out to stop the protesters on October 7 leading to a 9-hour standoff at Akashvani Bhawan where Rahul and Priyanka sat on a dharna, before they were forcibly removed. However, a day later the cops changed their strategy and allowed the opposition leaders led by Rahul Gandhi to offer prayers at Rajghat, Mahatma Gandhi's memorial. The leaders staged a sit-in to highlight what they alleged was "hijacking" of the country by Prime Minister Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and the CEC through a criminal conspiracy of "vote chori."On Friday, on the eve of CJP protests, the INDIA bloc MPs once again took to the streets, this time to Rashtrapati Bhawan to submit a memorandum to President Droupadi Murmu.The march, as expected, was stopped by the cops. The opposition leaders then sat on a dharna, this time at Vijay Chowk.The change in the street protests plan took even some of the INDIA bloc allies by surprise with some reports suggesting that allies were not happy over not being consulted. Not all of them were present for the extended street protests, leading to some uncomfortable questions about the INDIA bloc’s unity. Congress denied these charges.Congress leader Jairam Ramesh said all parties of the INDIA bloc had been invited, but the decision and communication came late on Tuesday night. "Therefore, it was natural that representatives from some parties could not participate in it. Some media outlets are making unnecessary comments about this," he posted on X.So, what prompted this change in protest plan? Was it the success of the October 6 march to Parliament protest that prompted the new strategy? Or, did the looming Cockroach Janata Party’s October 10 protest play a role in extending the INDIA bloc street action?To understand this, let’s rewind to June-July when youth came out in large numbers in several cities in response to the CJP’s agitation demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan as Union education minister against NEET paper leaks.The CJP, formed online in May by Abhijeet Dipke in response to a remark made by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant using terms "cockroaches" and "parasites" for those unemployed who attacked institutions through social media activism and litigation.On June 1, Dipke announced the first CJP protest for June 6 at Jantar Mantar in New Delhi. The next day, activist and educator Sonam Wangchuk joined the online movement. On June 6, the CJP launched physical demonstrations at Jantar Mantar. On 28 June 2026, Wangchuk joined the demonstration at Jantar Mantar and started an indefinite hunger strike demanding the resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.The agitation peaked on July 20, when students and youth from across the country marched to Jantar Mantar responding to CJP’s call. The Delhi police resorted to using unprecedented force to disperse the protesters. The political parties, which till then stood on the sidelines, tried to enter the protests. The Congress, which had focused on Rahul Gandhi’s “Chhatron ki Goonj” till then, staged a surprise protest outside Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s residence on July 21 to make its presence felt on the streets. However, the fulcrum of the anti-NEET paper leak protests remained the CJP, and the government was forced to accept its demand for resignation of Dharmendra Pradhan.With another CJP buildup in the making, the opposition parties led by the Congress perhaps don’t want to be “missing in action” this time around and leave the field open for the CJP. That could be one of the reasons why the INDIA bloc MPs have extended their stay on the streets.The Delhi Police have denied permission to the CJP for the October 10 Jantar Mantar protests citing short notice, past non-compliance with directions and concerns related to public safety, law and order and traffic regulation.But the CJP has announced to go ahead with its agitation. Abhijeet Dipke asserted that the protest would go ahead regardless of whether police permission was granted and said CJP activists were prepared to face arrest.Questioning the measures taken ahead of the protest, Dipke said, "What is this fear? Why are you this scared? You are scared of the youth in the country. You shut down trains, you shut down Metro, what should one do?"Earlier today, Delhi Police announced an unprecedented security clampdown on the national capital to prevent protesters from assembling for the agitation. The cops are also keeping an eye on over 200 content creators as part of the monitoring exercise. Police teams are examining online posts and messages relating to mobilisation, gathering points and the proposed demonstration.Later in the day, Supreme Court intervened and ordered Delhi police to ease some of the sweeping instructions to ensure that citizens, particularly those who have no intention of joining the ongoing demonstrations, were not inconvenienced. The top court said Metro and train services cannot be completely stopped and asked authorities to reconsider such restrictions in a proportionate manner.A bench led by Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and comprising Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana also clarified that the present proceedings primarily concern restrictions affecting the movement of ordinary citizens and public transport and not the broader right to protest.While the government and security forces will be closely watching the CJP's mobilisation on Saturday, the INDIA bloc will also be keeping an eagle's eye on how the youth respond. In July, the CJP managed to draw large crowds, leaving opposition parties struggling to make their presence felt.This time, the opposition has taken to the streets even before the CJP's planned protest. The question now is whether the INDIA bloc can match the CJP's mobilisation or whether the youth-led group will once again draw bigger crowds. The October 10 protest at Jantar Mantar may offer some answers.
Article Summary: Opposition leaders have hit the streets of the national capital, demanding removal of CEC Gyanesh Kumar over alleged irregularities in the SIR of electoral rolls. The opposition MPs, led by the Congress, returned to the streets with a march to Jantar Mantar on October 7, to Rajghat on October 8 and to Rashtrapati Bhawan on October 9.

Article Title: Can’t stop metro & trains, act as situation unfolds: Supreme Court to govt
Article Text:
Delhi Metro, trains to run amid CJP protest: SC says services can be regulated

SC: Issue a traffic advisory so that people don’t suffer

‘Jantar Mantar as protest site needs to change’

Poll Vote & Share your view Do you agree with the decision to allow metro and train services to continue amid protest concerns? Yes, it protects public convenience. No, safety should be prioritized. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Friday ordered govt not to stop Delhi metro services and trains heading to the capital on Saturday due to law and order “concerns” related to the anti-SIR protest planned by CJP, but said public transport services could be regulated depending on how the situation unfolds.Responding to a plea challenging govt’s decision on metro and train operations, a CJI-headed bench said it would inconvenience people dependent on public transport, and secured an assurance fr­om the solicitor general that there would be no blanket ban on movement of metro and trains reaching Delhi Saturday.The hearing saw the SC bench drive home their concern about proportionality by using the popular Hindi expression on using a hammer to swat a fly. Cautioned by SG Tushar Mehta that his remark could be misinterpreted, the bench clarified that they did not use the expression literally.In terms of that assurance, we direct competent authorities to allow plying of metro and trains in an appropriately regulated manner so as not to inconvenience public at large, and such decision may be given wide publicity to ensure citizens are aware of availability of the services,” said the bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana.“Similarly, appropriate traffic advisory is issued in newspapers and websites to enable people to avoid roads which are blocked and undertake travel inside the city. ”The bench focused on inconvenience likely to result from closure of public transport, and whether such a prohibition was required.Mehta had defended the su­spension of operations by te­rming it a regulated resp­o­nse to what he called an “em­e­r­ging law and order situation”.The urgent hearing that was allowed out of turn was marked by the absence of any challenge to Delhi Police’s denial of permission to CJP to hold an agitation against Special Intensive Revision of electoral rolls. “The only issue before us is whether the complete stoppage of metro and movement of trains requires reconsideration,” the judges told a team of senior advocates led by Kapil Sibal, who had sought the hearing.It was at 11.45am that the team of advocates made the mention in the interlude between two listed case hearings to complain that citizen’s fundamental right to peaceful protest was being strangled by orders of police and railways to shut down metro and rail services to Delhi.“How can this happen in our country,” Sibal asked and said he was appearing for CPM MP MA Baby. He was joined by senior advocates A M Singhvi, Prashant Bhushan, Vrinda Grover, Nithya Ramakrishna, N Hariharan and G Sankaranarayanan. The bench agreed to hear them but said someone from CJP, which has planned the protest, should appear. They held the urgent hearing despite CJP and other organisers of the protest not turning up at 2pm as promised by Sibal and the other advocates.SC asked Sibal and other counsel that “are any of you appearing for any of the organisers of the protest Saturday? Is Baby an organiser of the protest?” Sibal said his client was not an organiser. The bench asked have they sought permission to hold a protest. Bhushan responded they had sought permission much before but it was denied Friday morning.SC said the organisers needed to challenge the order of denial. “No doubt the right to form an association is a fundamental right, but that right must be exercised as per law. Once police deny permission, it needs to be challenged in court,” it said. “What is the ground reality with regard to protest? If it is with permission, it is a lawful protest. If it is not with permission, it is not in accordance with law. Even if it is not in accordance with law, we do not say people do not have a right to protest. But they are at the pain of prosecution,” the bench said.SG intervened to say CJP had in July sought permission to hold a day-long protest against the leak of NEET-UG papers, but stayed put at Jantar Mantar for 20 days.The bench kept its focus on the responsibility of organisers. “If we know who the organisers are, we can ask them what is the expected number of participants in the protest. We can regulate that and call upon the state to calibrate their responses not in a broad-spectrum way like complete stoppage of metro and rail service. But you say Baby is not an organiser,” the bench said.Sibal said, “I can come wi­th an organiser, but the court will say where is the order. By that time Oct 10 will be over. Allow us to represent an organiser and hear us at 2pm.” However, at 2pm, none of the organisers turned up.During the hearing, govt ag­r­eed with Sibal and other lawyers that the designated protest site needs to be ch­a­n­ged from Jantar Mantar to somewhere else. SG Mehta informed SC that he agreed wi­th their suggestions that govt soon take a decision to identify a designated protest venue instead of Jantar Mantar.The CJI-led bench said, “Govt and parties are agreeable to the suggestion that it is high time to identify and designate a proper protest site, instead of Jantar Mantar.... The competent authorities wo­uld consider the suggestion and take an appropriate decision.”
Article Summary: Supreme Court orders govt not to stop Delhi metro services and trains heading to the capital on Saturday due to law and order ‘concerns’ The bench said public transport services could be regulated depending on how the situation unfolds. The hearing saw the SC bench drive home their concern about proportionality by using the popular Hindi expression on using a hammer to swat a fly.

Article Title: Turning scandal into spotlight
Article Text:
‘

Paths of Glory’. It became

In 2009, I met Jeffrey Archer at Landmark, Chennai, when he came to India to launchone of my favourite Archer novels, inspired by the real-life story of British mountaineer George Mallory and his mysterious disappearance on Everest. I had my copy signed by him and remember the fan-girl moment.From school to college, hardly a month passed without an Archer short story or novel finding its way into my hands. His narration had one unmistakable signature—the twist in the tale. Over more than five decades, he built a global readership, with his books published in 114 countries and more than 47 languages, selling over 300 million copies.I can recall at least ten stories where the final turn makes you levitate from your chair. When I asked Archer at Landmark how he managed to write “like a machine”, he smiled. A writer without discipline, he said, will perish. His day began at six, followed by five hours of writing, from 6.30am to 11.30am, without calls, visitors or family interruptions. After that, the day was his.I also asked which Indian English writer he admired. Without hesitation, he said, ‘ R K Narayan ’. Archer’s admiration for Narayan’s ability to bring Indian life alive through English was immediate.Mallory, the main character in ‘Paths of Glory’, disappeared on Everest in 1924 while attempting to reach the summit. Whether he became the first man to climb the Everest remains unknown. His body was discovered 75 years later, a few 100 metres below the summit. Among his belongings, one object was missing—the photograph of his wife, Ruth. Mallory had promised Ruth that if he reached the summit, he would leave her photograph there. Did he reach the top and keep his promise? Nobody knows.That is Archer at his finest: research, suspense, emotion and an unexpected clue, stitched together with the elegance of a master storyteller.Archer’s own life contained twists no novelist could resist. At the height of his fame, he was a parliamentarian and a close associate of Margaret Thatcher. After a newspaper accused him of paying a sex worker, he won a libel case in 1987. But it later emerged that he had lied in court. In 2001, he was sentenced to four years for perjury. His political career ended.But his story did not.In prison, he kept a 1,001 page journal, later published as ‘A Prison Diary’. After his release came ‘Cat O’Nine Tales’, stories inspired by fellow prisoners. Betrayal, justice and second chances began to echo through his writing.What fascinates me most is his alchemy: he turned disgrace into material, confinement into creativity and a public fall into a second literary ascent.Valluvar says in Kural 240:“Vasai Ozhiya Vaazhvaare VaazhvarIsaiyozhiya Vaazhvaare Vaazhadhavar.”“Those who live free of blame truly live; Those who live without renown have not truly lived.”Archer’s life complicates that wisdom. Here was a man who knew blame, disgrace and downfall—and yet transformed them into another kind of grace.Perhaps that is the most Archer-like twist of all: the story was not over with the fall. He simply turned the page.
Article Summary: Jeffrey Archer's books published in 114 countries and more than 47 languages, selling over 300 million copies. His narration had one unmistakable signature—the twist in the tale. At the height of his fame, he was a parliamentarian and close associate of Margaret Thatcher.

Article Title: Presidential election today? Trump confuses India with Brazil, claims 125 million voted
Article Text:
Trump says "125 million Indians voted in presidential election today."

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

US President Donald Trump on Monday confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian “presidential election”, while also questioning the integrity of the American voting system.In a post on Truth Social, Trump wrote, “125 Million People voted today in the first round of India’s Presidential Election. The results came out shortly after the vote closed, on the same day!”He then compared the alleged election results with the US electoral process, writing, “In Detroit, Philadelphia, California, and numerous other US Cities and States, the results, with much smaller numbers, will often take weeks to Rig, I mean, calculate. Voting in America is corrupt!!!”However, India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college and not through a direct nationwide popular vote.Trump's remarks came after Brazil held the first round of its presidential election on Sunday, with incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and right-wing challenger Flávio Bolsonaro advancing to the October 25 runoff.With 99.99% of the votes counted, Bolsonaro secured 47.03% of the valid votes, while Lula received 45.16%, according to Brazil's Superior Electoral Court.The figure of around 125 million mentioned by Trump is close to Brazil's total valid votes, which stood at about 125.27 million, suggesting he may have confused the Brazilian election with India.Neither Bolsonaro nor Lula crossed the 50% threshold required to win in the first round, triggering the October 25 runoff, BBC reported.Flávio Bolsonaro, the son of former Brazilian president Jair Bolsonaro, outperformed expectations in the first round and finished ahead of Lula. His strong showing has raised the prospect of a shift to the right in Latin America's largest economy.Brazil has used electronic voting for decades, and electoral authorities said the first-round voting process proceeded smoothly.The Organization of American States' electoral observation mission said “the voting has been going smoothly and under adequate safety conditions.”The rapid announcement of results has also been cited as a strength of Brazil's electronic voting system.“When results take a lot of time, it creates an opening for people to cast doubt on the results, to say there’s been a problem,” Josemar Lauriano Pereira, a 46-year-old lawyer in Rio de Janeiro, told the Associated Press.Trump's post drew reactions on social media, with users pointing out that India does not elect its president through a direct popular vote.One user posted, “Trump living in a different world? Is a presidential election taking place in India? President Donald Trump made the incorrect claim that 125 million people voted in India's "presidential election" today.”Another said, “What is my blud Donald Trump smoking? Why is he mentioning India instead of Brazil when talking about the election?”
Article Summary: US President Donald Trump confused India with Brazil, claiming that 125 million people had voted in an Indian "presidential election" He also questioned the integrity of the American voting system. India did not hold a presidential election on Sunday. The President of India is elected indirectly by an electoral college.

Article Title: SIR strikes at heart of Constitution: Supreme Court judge Ujjal Bhuyan
Article Text:
File photo: Supreme Court of India Judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan (PTI Photo)

-

Detaching right to vote from citizen is like taking soul out of body: Bhuyan

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Launching a scathing attack on special intensive revision (SIR) that has resulted in large-scale deletion of names from voter lists across states, Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan on Sunday said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution.Discounting the reasons given by govt and EC to justify SIR, which was upheld in the case of the revision of rolls in West Bengal by SC with modifications, Justice Bhuyan said, "No amount of whataboutery can justify it. It strikes at the very heart of Constitution. I would go to the extent of saying that it is a negation of the constitutional order which we have adopted under the Constitution."He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad.Nalsar students, who had opposed CJI Surya Kant's participation in the convocation ceremony recently, came in for praise from Justice Bhuyan.Also read| Democracy in peril as voters illegally ousted: Former SC judge Justice Rohinton Fali Nariman "One last word about the brilliant students of Nalsar. You have shown to the country and to the world what a university student, that too a student of law, should be. You are brilliant, you are bold, and you are brave," he said.Justice Bhuyan said a citizen’s right to vote was central to the holding of free and fair elections.“Except in the case of a dead voter, the name of a voter once enlisted in the electoral roll cannot be deleted without notice and hearing,” he added.The SC judge said the right to vote or be included in the voters’ list could not be detached from the persona of an Indian citizen.Also read: EC orders special drive to add genuine electors 'left out' during SIR “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added. Justice Bhuyan said the Indian Constitution does not provide for two classes of citizens: citizens with voting rights and citizens without voting rights. “Any process which leads to wholesale disenfranchisement of Indian citizens, making them citizens without voting rights, would be violative of Articles 326 and 14 of Constitution of India,” he said.“If any process results in disenfranchising millions and millions of Indian citizens, making them second class citizens in their own country in the sense of being citizens without voting rights, such a process is intrinsically arbitrary,” he added, his remarks coinciding with attacks on EC and govt over SIR by the opposition and others.Justice Bhuyan said the right to vote was intertwined with India’s years of struggle against foreign rule. “It is a manifestation of our freedom achieved after so much struggle and sacrifice. Article 326 (universal adult franchise) cannot be tinkered with at all. No authority can do it, no court can condone it. No one is above Constitution,” he said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court judge Justice Ujjal Bhuyan said any process disenfranchising millions of Indian citizens was intrinsically arbitrary as it struck at the heart of the Constitution. He was speaking at the moot court valedictory function at Nalsar, Hyderabad. “If it is done, it will be like taking out the soul from the body,” he added.

Article Title: How Neeraj Chopra's javelin helped Rohit Yadav win Asian Games bronze
Article Text:
Rohit Yadav (Image credit: X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: When Rohit Yadav stepped onto the field in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan, for the Asian Games javelin final, he carried more than a piece of sporting equipment. In his hand was a signed javelin belonging to Olympic and world champion Neeraj Chopra — a quiet gesture of support that would accompany him to an international podium.The story began in June, when Yadav struck gold at the National Inter State Senior Athletics Championships in Bhubaneswar with a personal best of 87.05m. Upon returning to his training base in NIS Patiala, he discovered that his preferred javelin had bent, apparently during air transit in its protective PVC tube in the aircraft’s cargo hold.Yadav subsequently competed at the Commonwealth Games in Glasgow with a borrowed implement, finishing seventh with 81.56m in cold, windy conditions. With the Asian Games approaching, he faced the prospect of competing without his trusted javelin.“For the Asian Games, I didn’t have my own javelin. My preferred one was damaged and had bent. While coming to Delhi from Patiala for the Indian Athletics Final Series on Sept 10, I spoke to Neeraj bhai,” Yadav told TOI.“We have been in regular touch. I knew he had returned to India for rehabilitation. I told him I didn’t have a javelin of my own for the Asian Games.He immediately came to my rescue and sent me one of his signed javelins through a private taxi service to the Jawaharlal Nehru (JLN) stadium,” he added.Chopra had withdrawn from the remainder of the season, including the Asian Games, to recover from an ankle ligament injury. His absence left India without its two-time defending champion, but his gesture ensured that a fellow Indian thrower had the equipment he needed.There was, however, a catch. Yadav could not use the javelin in Delhi because it had not been registered with the Technical Information Centre (TIC) for inspection. He borrowed another registered implement for the event, then carefully packed Chopra’s gift for Japan.“At the Asian Games, I registered two javelins with the TIC. But I used the one Neeraj bhai gave me. I had a good grip and hold over it, and with that javelin I made the winning throw to secure bronze with 84.35m,” he said.“I will remain thankful to Neeraj bhai. I have kept that javelin with me and will use it in future competitions as well.”After his competition, Rohit listened to Chopra’s congratulatory voice message.“He told me to enjoy the win and savour my first big international medal. He said that when he returns fully fit, we will compete together, and that I have a long way to go.”Back home in Uttar Pradesh’s Jaunpur, Yadav is taking the off-season to spend time with family until Diwali.“I want to earn a Diamond League entry, compete internationally and qualify for the World Championships next year. The ultimate target remains the Los Angeles Olympics,” he added.
Article Summary: Rohit Yadav won bronze at the Asian Games in Aichi-Nagoya, Japan. Yadav used a signed javelin belonging to Olympic and world champion Neeraj Chopra. Chopra had withdrawn from the remainder of the season to recover from an ankle ligament injury.

Article Title: "I know how hard she works”: How Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle turned a business struggle into a five-venture empire while building her own path beyond the NHL spotlight
Article Text:
Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle turned a business struggle into a five-venture empire(Image via X)

Connor McDavid saw how hard Lauren Kyle was working behind the scenes

Lauren Kyle used that lesson to expand far beyond interior design

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Lauren Kyle McDavid had always known she wanted to build something of her own, but turning her creative ideas into successful businesses came with a learning curve. The wife of Edmonton Oilers captain Connor McDavid started with interior design before expanding into fashion, furniture, food and publishing. Behind that growth was a challenge she had to face early in her career: learning the business side of her creative work.That part of Lauren’s journey became more important as she took on more projects. By June 2025, she had several ventures under her name, while Connor had watched closely as she learned to turn her ideas into businesses. His support also came at a time when Lauren needed help taking her first company to the next level.Lauren Kyle spoke about her entrepreneurial journey in a June 8, 2025 interview with theScore. She explained that she had always pictured herself working for herself and had grown up around people who ran their own businesses. Her first major venture was Kyle & Co., an interior design company that gave her a place to turn her ideas into a career.However, creativity alone could not handle every part of running a growing company.Connor explained during the same theScore interview that creative people can sometimes struggle with the business side of their ideas. He had seen Lauren put considerable time and energy into Kyle & Co. and wanted to help her move the company forward.“I know how hard she works, and I know the time and energy that she puts into it,” Connor said while discussing Lauren’s business journey with theScore in June 2025.Connor McDavid had also given Lauren sessions with a business coach as a birthday gift a few years earlier. The support proved useful because Lauren wanted to grow beyond her first company without losing the creative side that had driven her from the beginning.Lauren later explained just how valuable that experience became for her. “Without my business coach, I definitely wouldn't be able to have this many businesses at one time,” she told theScore in June 2025. She said the coaching helped change her mindset and gave her a better understanding of how to grow as an entrepreneur.The business coaching became part of a much bigger change in Lauren’s career. By June 2025, her portfolio included Kyle & Co., Sports Club Atelier, Trove Living and Bar Trove, while she was also preparing a cookbook.Sports Club Atelier grew from Lauren’s interest in creating better-looking sports apparel. Trove Living gave her interior design work a furniture and showroom component, while Bar Trove brought her creative approach into the restaurant space in downtown Edmonton. Her cookbook followed the same idea by focusing on experiences such as dinner parties and girls’ weekends instead of simply dividing recipes into traditional categories.Lauren’s approach has remained consistent across those projects. She wants people to feel something when they enter a space, wear something she designed or experience something she created. That idea also explains why Connor has remained impressed by the work happening behind the scenes.“I get a front row seat to everything she’s building,” Connor said in theScore’s June 2025 profile.Lauren’s story is therefore about more than being Connor McDavid’s wife. She had to learn a side of business that did not come naturally to her, accepted help when she needed it and used that experience to build a much larger portfolio of her own.
Article Summary: Connor McDavid’s wife Lauren Kyle turned a business struggle into a five-venture empire. By June 2025, her portfolio included Kyle & Co., Sports Club Atelier, Trove Living and Bar Trove. Connor McDavid had also given Lauren sessions with a business coach as a birthday gift.

Article Title: Jessica Pegula’s tennis career is only part of her family story: Inside her relationship with Taylor Gahagen to life away from the court and more

Jessica Pegula’s tennis career is only part of her family story: Inside her relationship with Taylor Gahagen to life away from the court and more

Details on Jessica Pegula and Taylor Gahagen’s relationship, marriage and life beyond tennis

Taylor Gahagen supports Jessica Pegula’s tennis journey

Jessica Pegula balances family, business and philanthropy

Jessica Pegula is one of the best American players of her generation. But she’s so much more than tournament wins and WTA rankings. Pegula, a Buffalo, New York native, is the daughter of Terry and Kim Pegula, owners of the Buffalo Bills and Buffalo Sabres, and comes from a family with deep roots in professional sports. She has made a career out of her own exploits on the tennis circuit.Away from competition, Pegula has also built a life with Taylor Gahagen, a businessman who has remained a close and largely private presence throughout her rise. Their relationship began years before their marriage, and Gahagen has since become involved in several aspects of Pegula’s life, including her business interests and philanthropic work. Their partnership has developed alongside Pegula’s demanding international tennis schedule.Jessica Pegula and Taylor Gahagen first became linked publicly around 2015. Their relationship developed while Gahagen was working for Pegula Sports and Entertainment, the organisation associated with Pegula’s parents. Gahagen had already established a career in the sports-business environment, giving the pair a professional connection before their relationship became a significant part of their personal lives.The couple became engaged by early 2019 and initially planned to marry in 2020. Those plans were delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, eventually pushing their wedding back by a year. In October 2021, Pegula and Gahagen finally married at the Biltmore Estate in Asheville, North Carolina, surrounded by family, friends and several members of Pegula’s tennis circle.Their marriage has remained relatively private compared with the public attention surrounding Pegula’s professional career. Gahagen is regularly described as an important support figure, travelling with Pegula when possible while maintaining his own professional responsibilities away from the tennis spotlight. The couple also eventually found time for a honeymoon in Costa Rica in 2022, after Pegula’s demanding playing schedule made immediate travel difficult.Gahagen’s role in Pegula’s life goes beyond that of a spouse, and his background in business and sports management has given him an understanding of the pressures surrounding professional athletics. Before moving into other ventures, he worked for nearly a decade at Pegula Sports and Entertainment, where he held several positions before becoming an executive. He left the organisation in 2023 and later became a managing partner at Dragos Capital and Agarwood Wealth.His support has also been visible around Pegula’s tennis career, and with tournaments requiring constant travel, training and preparation, having a trusted person nearby can provide stability away from competition. Pegula has spoken about having a strong support system, while reports have highlighted Gahagen’s presence around her during major events.Pegula’s tennis résumé has continued to grow during their marriage. The WTA lists her career-high singles ranking as No 3 and records multiple WTA singles titles, including victories in Charleston and Dubai in 2026. She has also enjoyed substantial success in doubles, including titles with Coco Gauff.The relationship has therefore developed alongside some of the biggest stages of Pegula’s career. Rather than becoming a highly publicised celebrity partnership, Pegula and Gahagen have generally kept their personal life understated while allowing their professional achievements to remain the focus.Pegula’s family background remains another major part of her story. Her parents, Terry and Kim Pegula, became prominent figures in American professional sports through their ownership of the Buffalo Bills and Buffalo Sabres. That connection has naturally placed Pegula under additional attention, but her tennis career has developed independently through years of training and competition.Her family life has also included difficult periods, and Kim Pegula experienced a serious health crisis in 2022, and Jessica later discussed the impact of her mother’s condition while continuing to compete at the highest level. The experience added another dimension to Pegula’s public story, demonstrating the challenge of balancing major family circumstances with the demands of professional tennis.Outside tennis, Pegula has developed entrepreneurial interests. She founded Ready 24, a skincare company designed around active lifestyles, with Gahagen also involved in the venture. The brand focuses on straightforward skincare products for people with demanding or active routines. Gahagen has served as vice president of the company, giving the couple another professional project alongside their personal relationship.Their philanthropic work has become another important part of their life away from tennis. Pegula and Gahagen co-founded A Lending Paw, an organisation focused on helping rescue dogs receive training that can prepare them to become service animals for people in need. The initiative reflects their shared interest in animal welfare while connecting rescued animals with people who require assistance.The organisation has continued to attract outside support. In 2026, The Farmer’s Dog announced a multi-year partnership supporting A Lending Paw’s mission to help more rescue dogs receive care, nutrition and training before becoming service animals. Pegula has also been identified as the owner of three rescue dogs, Maddie, Des and Mabel, reinforcing the personal connection behind the initiative.Pegula’s life away from tennis consequently combines family, entrepreneurship and philanthropy rather than simply revolving around her status as a professional athlete. Her marriage to Gahagen is an important part of that balance, particularly because their shared projects allow their professional and charitable interests to overlap.While tennis remains the centre of Pegula’s public career, her wider story has continued to develop in parallel. Her relationship with Gahagen has provided a private foundation during an increasingly demanding period of competition, while their work through Ready 24 and A Lending Paw has given them shared interests outside sport.Pegula’s family connections may have introduced her to the world of professional sports from an early age, but her achievements have been shaped by her own career. Her rise to a career-high No 3 ranking, WTA titles and deep runs at major tournaments have established her as a significant figure in American tennis.Together, these elements show why Pegula’s story cannot be reduced to tennis alone, and her marriage, family experiences, business interests and charitable commitments provide a broader picture of an athlete building a life both within and beyond professional competition.
Article Summary: Jessica Pegula married Taylor Gahagen in October 2021. Pegula is the daughter of Terry and Kim Pegula, owners of the Buffalo Bills and Buffalo Sabres. The couple became engaged in early 2019 and initially planned to marry in 2020. Their plans were delayed by the COVID-19 pandemic, eventually pushing their wedding back by a year.

Article Title: Legend Mike Ditka dies at 86 after building a rare Chicago Bears legacy as Hall of Fame player and Super Bowl-winning coach
Article Text:
Mike Ditka, a Pro Football Hall of Fame tight end who later coached the Chicago Bears to victory in Super Bowl XX, has died at 86. (Image via Getty)

What made Mike Ditka’s Chicago Bears legacy so unusual?

How did Mike Ditka remain part of NFL culture after his coaching career?

Mike Ditka, the Hall of Fame tight end who later returned to lead the Chicago Bears to the franchise’s only Super Bowl championship, has died at 86.Ditka’s family announced his death Friday, Oct. 9, in a statement shared by Jarrett Payton, the son of Bears legend Walter Payton. ESPN reported that no cause of death had been announced.“It is with profound sadness that we announce the passing of our beloved husband, father, grandfather, and friend, Mike Ditka,” the family said. “While the world knew Mike as a Hall of Fame football player, legendary coach, and leader of the Chicago Bears' Super Bowl XX championship team, we knew him as the heart of our family.”The statement continued: “Mike will be missed beyond measure and remembered forever.”Ditka did not build his place in Bears history from one sideline.Chicago selected him fifth overall in the 1961 NFL Draft. He immediately changed expectations for his position, becoming the first tight end to record more than 1,000 receiving yards in a season while earning Rookie of the Year honors.Ditka spent six seasons with the Bears and made five consecutive Pro Bowls. He was also part of Chicago’s 1963 NFL championship team before later playing for the Philadelphia Eagles and Dallas Cowboys.His playing career included another championship with Dallas in Super Bowl VI. In 1988, Ditka became the first tight end inducted into the Pro Football Hall of Fame.By then, however, he had already started building an entirely separate legacy in Chicago.After nine seasons as an assistant under Tom Landry in Dallas, Ditka returned to the Bears as head coach in 1982. He took Chicago to the playoffs seven times across 11 seasons and reached three NFC Championship Games.Nothing defined that run more than the 1985 team.The Bears went 15-1 in the regular season behind a defense that remains one of the most celebrated units in NFL history. Chicago then overwhelmed the New England Patriots 46-10 in Super Bowl XX.Ditka had now won championships with the Bears as both a player and head coach.That distinction explains why his connection with Chicago lasted far beyond his final game on the sideline.The Bears fired Ditka following the 1992 season, but his football career continued.He returned to head coaching with the New Orleans Saints in 1997. Ditka went 15-33 across three seasons, and his tenure became closely associated with the blockbuster 1999 trade for Ricky Williams.New Orleans sent Washington eight draft picks, including two first-round selections, to move up and select Williams fifth overall.Ditka’s influence eventually moved from the sideline to television. He worked as an NFL analyst for NBC and later ESPN, including a long run on ESPN’s “Sunday NFL Countdown.”His profile also extended beyond traditional football coverage.“Saturday Night Live” built its recurring “Bill Swerski’s Superfans” sketches around exaggerated devotion to Ditka and “Da Bears.” He appeared in commercials, television programs and the 2005 film “Kicking and Screaming.”That visibility never replaced what made Ditka matter in football. It grew out of it.He finished his NFL playing career with 427 receptions, 5,812 receiving yards and 43 touchdowns. He became a Hall of Famer at a position he helped redefine, then returned to Chicago and coached one of the NFL’s most recognizable championship teams.Few careers allow one person to become part of a franchise’s history twice.Ditka did it in Chicago.
Article Summary: Ditka’s family announced his death Friday, Oct. 9, in a statement shared by Jarrett Payton, the son of Bears legend Walter Payton. Ditka spent six seasons with the Bears and made five consecutive Pro Bowls. He took Chicago to the playoffs seven times across 11 seasons and reached three NFC Championship Games.

Article Title: Jon Jones finally remembers longtime “frenemy” Daniel Cormier after struggling through hilarious pizza challenge

Their rivalry featured heated exchanges, a famous media-day brawl and two championship fights. Article Title: How did Jason Kelce go from criticising NFL referees to defending them? His stance shifted after two controversial incidents
Article Text:
Jason Kelce go from criticising NFL referees to defending them(Getty)

Jason Kelce initially backed Eric Wilson after his clash with Adrian Hill

Trey McBride incident and NFL referee suspensions spark a wider debate

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Jason Kelce had plenty to say about the NFL ’s decision to suspend two officials after separate on-field incidents involving Trey McBride and Eric Wilson. The retired Philadelphia Eagles center initially criticised referee Adrian Hill for his treatment of Wilson during the Minnesota Vikings’ game against the Miami Dolphins. However, Kelce later changed his position during an episode of New Heights, the podcast he hosts with his brother, Travis Kelce The debate grew after the NFL suspended Hill for one game and line judge Jeff Seeman for two games on Oct. 5, 2026. Both officials faced discipline for what the league described as unprofessional conduct toward a player. Kelce’s change of stance added another twist to a controversy that has raised questions about how the NFL should hold officials accountable when tempers flare during games.During the Vikings-Dolphins game in Week 4, Miami running back Ollie Gordon II knocked Minnesota linebacker Eric Wilson into Hill, sending the referee to the ground. Hill got back up and shouted at Wilson, who appeared to be trying to help him stand.Kelce criticised the official’s response during New Heights, arguing that Wilson had not deliberately knocked Hill down. He said, “I have a bigger problem with this one.'Cause clearly Eric Wilson did not try to do this. And then he’s trying to help him up, and then he gets mad at him. I think this is bogus.”His initial reaction focused on the circumstances behind the collision. Wilson had not appeared to intentionally bring Hill down, yet the exchange escalated after the official got back to his feet. The incident became one of two high-profile officiating controversies that prompted the NFL to review its officials’ conduct.However, Kelce did not stick with that position for long. Later in the same podcast discussion, he reconsidered his response and announced that he was retracting his criticism.“You know what? I’m retracting all this! I’m on the sides of both of these officials! I take the officials’ side!” Kelce said on New Heights””.His reversal gave the discussion a new direction, especially as the NFL faced criticism over the punishments handed to Hill and Seeman.The other controversy involved Seeman and Arizona Cardinals tight end Trey McBride. During Arizona’s 36-24 loss to the New York Giants, Seeman appeared to direct profanity at McBride after a third-down incompletion. McBride had disputed the lack of a pass-interference penalty against Giants cornerback Dru Phillips.Video of the exchange circulated online before the NFL announced Seeman’s two-game suspension on October 5. Hill received a one-game suspension for his interaction with Wilson.The NFL Referees Association challenged the severity of the penalties. On Tuesday, October 6, executive director Scott Green acknowledged that the officials’ conduct fell short of professional standards but argued that referees regularly face heated exchanges and verbal abuse from players and coaches.The NFL Players Association took a firmer stance on Seeman’s conduct. Executive director JC Tretter said officials should face the same standards as players when they cross the line.The league has disciplined players for their treatment of officials, too. In October 2025, Denver Broncos linebacker Dre Greenlaw received a one-game suspension without pay after chasing referee Brad Allen and verbally threatening him following Denver’s 33-32 win over the New York Giants. His appeal failed.Kelce’s change of heart did not settle the argument. Instead, it highlighted the difficult balance between protecting officials and holding them accountable. With the referees’ union challenging the suspensions, the NFL now faces further scrutiny over how it handles misconduct on both sides of the whistle.
Article Summary: Jason Kelce initially criticised referee Adrian Hill for his treatment of Eric Wilson during the Minnesota Vikings’ game against the Miami Dolphins. However, Kelce later changed his position during an episode of New Heights, the podcast he hosts with his brother, Travis Kelce. The debate grew after the NFL suspended Hill for one game and line judge Jeff Seeman for two games on October 5, 2026.

Article Title: Never give up! Nic Maddinson’s remarkable journey from testicular cancer and chemotherapy to an unexpected Australia Test comeback
Article Text:
Nic Maddinson (X)

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

When Nic Maddinson told his four-year-old son August that he was heading to South Africa, the youngster began listing the animals he knew lived there. The family even squeezed in some cricket in the hallway of their Byron Bay home before Maddinson left for what could become one of the most significant chapters of his career.For the left-handed batter, however, the journey back to Australia’s Test team has been about far more than cricket. It has been a story of battling testicular cancer, enduring chemotherapy and finding a new perspective on life before earning an unexpected return to the national set-up.Maddinson discovered a lump last year, and scans revealed testicular cancer. He underwent surgery to remove it, but further tests seven weeks later showed the cancer had spread to parts of his abdominal lymph nodes and lung.At the time, his wife Bianca was pregnant with their second child. She gave up her job as a dentist to care for their toddler, August, while Maddinson underwent treatment.His days became a difficult routine of hospital visits, rest and trying to eat before attempting to sleep again. He completed chemotherapy on July 14, but had to wait another two months before receiving clearance to resume full training.The birth of his second son, Wilder, brought another source of joy as Maddinson began rebuilding his life and cricket career.Having come through the ordeal, he has also urged others to seek medical attention if they notice anything unusual.His return to competitive cricket has been remarkable. Maddinson last played first-class cricket in March 2025, meaning he went 579 days without a match in the format before returning to Australia's Test set-up. It is the longest such gap for an Australian before a men's Test match.The call-up itself came as a surprise. When George Bailey , the chair of selectors, rang him, Maddinson initially wondered whether the conversation might concern an Australia A tour of India or another young player.“I thought maybe he was calling me to go to India for the A tour or ask about another young player around because I was a little bit unsure what was going on,” Maddinson said.He admitted he had not believed himself to be close to a Test recall, although the hope of returning had never disappeared.“Obviously didn't feel like I was that close but still had hopes of maybe one day getting back into a Test squad. So, in terms of motivation, it's still always been there but yeah definitely a bit of a surprise.”The 34-year-old spent much of the long flight to South Africa processing the news, trying to relax with sleep and films while reflecting on what he described as one of the “craziest” weekends of his life.Despite the lengthy break from first-class cricket, Maddinson said he was confident about his physical conditioning. He had been playing matches and multi-day red-ball games with New South Wales as he worked towards regaining his fitness.His outlook on cricket has also changed since his previous Test appearance against Pakistan at the MCG in 2016. A decade of first-class experience, combined with his health battle, has helped him find greater balance and confidence in his game.“I always felt like I understood the game pretty well but when you look back I feel like you probably don't know that much,” he said.He believes he has learnt not to force himself into a particular style simply to satisfy selectors or secure his place in the side, instead developing the ability to adapt to different conditions.Now back in the Test environment, Maddinson has been welcomed by teammates who know him from years of playing alongside or against him. His return also reunites him with coach Andrew McDonald, under whom he honed his skills during his time in Victoria.The comeback is already a powerful story of resilience. After cancer treatment, a lengthy absence from first-class cricket and the uncertainty of whether another Test opportunity would come, Maddinson has earned his way back.For August, the trip may be about South Africa’s animals and geography. For his father, it represents something far bigger: a return to the game after overcoming a battle that put life itself into perspective.
Article Summary: Nic Maddinson has returned to Australia's Test set-up. The 34-year-old last played first-class cricket in March 2025. It is the longest such gap for an Australian before a men's Test match. Maddinson discovered a lump last year, and scans revealed testicular cancer.

Article Title: Travis Kelce joins Cleveland Guardians ownership group as $1.7 billion MLB franchise adds a new chapter to his hometown legacy
Article Text:
Travis Kelce joins Cleveland Guardians ownership group as $1.7 billion MLB franchise adds a new chapter to his hometown legacy

What do we know about Travis Kelce’s investment in the Cleveland Guardians?

How much are the Cleveland Guardians worth, and what could Kelce’s stake be worth?

Will Travis Kelce have any control over the Guardians’ players and baseball decisions?

Why does the Guardians investment matter to Kelce’s hometown and his growing business portfolio?

New Heights

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Travis Kelce has built a successful career in the NFL, but his interests now extend beyond football. In May 2026, the Kansas City Chiefs tight end became a minority investor in the Cleveland Guardians, giving him a financial connection to the Major League Baseball team he grew up supporting. The investment brings his professional success closer to his hometown roots, but questions remain about how much he paid, what percentage he owns, and whether his involvement could influence the franchise’s future. While the financial details remain private, the deal offers an interesting look at how professional athletes are turning their earnings and public profiles into long-term business investments.The Cleveland Guardians announced Kelce’s minority investment on May 27, 2026, marking a new chapter in the relationship between the NFL star and his hometown. The announcement came before the team’s game against the Washington Nationals, bringing attention to a deal that connected one of football’s most recognizable players with Cleveland’s baseball franchise.Kelce purchased a minority interest from the ownership group associated with David Blitzer. Blitzer holds a 35% stake in the Guardians, making his position an important part of the team’s ownership structure.However, this does not mean Kelce purchased 35% of the franchise. The reported transaction involved a portion of Blitzer’s interest, and the exact percentage acquired by Kelce has not been publicly disclosed.The distinction matters because ownership percentages determine the financial value of an investment and the rights that come with it. Without knowing Kelce’s exact share, it is not possible to establish his ownership value, calculate his expected returns, or determine how much of the team’s business he owns.The purchase price has also remained private. Neither Kelce nor the Guardians has announced the amount paid for the investment. As a result, figures circulating about his personal spending should not be treated as confirmed unless they can be supported by reliable reporting or an official disclosure.The transaction nevertheless gives Kelce a direct financial interest in a major professional baseball franchise. Instead of simply attending games or supporting the team as a celebrity fan, he now has a business connection to the organization.For Cleveland, the investment also brings an internationally recognized sports personality closer to the Guardians brand. Kelce’s NFL career, public appearances, and business activities give him a profile that extends beyond football. His involvement can attract attention to the baseball team, although the actual financial impact of that attention cannot be measured from the ownership announcement alone.The Guardians’ reported valuation provides useful context for understanding why the investment has attracted attention. Forbes estimated the franchise’s value at approximately $1.7 billion around the time of the announcement, with other reports placing the figure in a similar range. The valuation reflects the broader business value of the franchise, rather than the amount Kelce paid for his individual share.The Guardians were valued at approximately $1 billion in 2022, when Blitzer first invested in the organization. Comparing that figure with the later estimate of roughly $1.7 billion suggests a substantial increase in the franchise’s reported value over four years.That rise is significant because professional sports teams can become valuable long-term assets. Their businesses are supported by several sources of income, including broadcasting agreements, ticket sales, sponsorships, merchandise, stadium-related revenue, and other commercial partnerships. The exact mix varies by franchise, and a team’s overall valuation does not mean all of that value is immediately available as cash to its owners.A higher franchise valuation can benefit existing investors if they eventually sell their shares at a favorable price. However, an increase in estimated value does not automatically translate into a realized profit. The final return depends on the purchase price, ownership percentage, operating costs, financial obligations, and the terms of a future sale.For Kelce, the absence of a disclosed ownership percentage makes it impossible to calculate a reliable value for his investment. For example, a hypothetical 1% interest in a franchise valued at $1.7 billion would correspond to $17 million before considering transaction terms and other adjustments. That is only an illustration of the mathematics, not a claim that Kelce owns 1% or invested $17 million.The same caution applies to estimates of how much money he might earn from the deal. The Guardians have not disclosed Kelce’s investment terms, any special financial arrangements, or the returns he could receive. It would therefore be inaccurate to describe a particular amount as his confirmed investment or expected profit.The most reliable conclusion is that Kelce has acquired an undisclosed minority interest in a franchise whose reported value is around $1.7 billion. That makes the deal potentially significant, but its precise financial value to him remains unknown.Kelce’s investment does not make him the person responsible for running the Cleveland Guardians. His position as a minority investor is different from the role of a controlling owner, team president, general manager, or manager. These positions carry different responsibilities, and owning a portion of a franchise does not automatically give an investor authority over its baseball operations.The Dolan family remains the Guardians’ controlling ownership group. Its position is important because control of a sports franchise generally determines who has the final say over major organizational decisions. Kelce’s reported investment does not replace the existing ownership structure or give him control over the team.Decisions involving player contracts, trades, recruitment, coaching appointments, payroll, and long-term baseball strategy remain matters for the organization’s established leadership. There is no confirmed information indicating that Kelce will have direct authority over these decisions.This distinction is especially important when a celebrity becomes involved with a sports franchise. The public may associate a famous investor with the team and assume that the person will influence its future. In reality, an investor’s involvement depends on the rights attached to the shares they purchase and the agreements governing the ownership group.The Guardians have also been connected to a separate ownership development involving Blitzer. His 35% interest comes with an option to pursue majority control after the 2027 season. However, an option is not the same as a completed transaction. It gives its holder a potential route to a future deal, subject to the applicable terms, rather than guaranteeing that control will change hands.Kelce’s investment should therefore be understood within the existing ownership arrangement. His financial interest connects him to the franchise, but there is no confirmed basis for saying he will decide which players the Guardians sign, how much they spend on their roster, or who leads their baseball operations.His most visible contribution may instead come through his public profile and relationship with the city. A well-known athlete supporting a local team can attract media coverage, strengthen community connections, and introduce the franchise to audiences who might not regularly follow baseball. Those possibilities make the investment interesting without requiring Kelce to take on a management role.For Kelce, the Guardians investment carries a personal connection that goes beyond the financial value of the franchise. He grew up in Northeast Ohio and attended Cleveland Heights High School, where baseball was part of his sporting background before football became the centre of his professional career.His connection to Cleveland has remained part of his public identity even after establishing himself with the Kansas City Chiefs. The investment gives him a way to maintain that connection while participating in the business side of professional sports.The Guardians described Kelce as someone with a deep affection for Cleveland and Northeast Ohio. Kelce, in turn, presented the opportunity as a chance to strengthen his lasting connection with the city’s east side. These statements help explain the personal meaning of the deal, although they do not reveal its financial terms.The investment also fits into Kelce’s wider business activities. Beyond his NFL career, he has developed commercial interests and partnerships in areas such as entertainment, consumer brands, and sports. His business portfolio has included ventures associated with Garage Beer, investments connected to entertainment and hospitality, and thepodcast, which he co-hosts with his brother, Jason Kelce.These activities show how a professional athlete can build income sources and business relationships beyond a playing contract. An athlete’s career on the field is limited by factors such as age, performance, injuries, and contract opportunities. Investments, by contrast, can potentially continue to hold value after the athlete retires, although they also carry financial risks.Owning a minority share of a baseball franchise offers a different opportunity from endorsing a product. An endorsement generally involves promoting a brand in exchange for compensation, while an equity investment gives the investor an ownership interest in a business. The potential financial outcome depends on the business’s performance, the value of the shares, and the terms of the investment.There may also be a branding benefit for the Guardians. Kelce’s popularity gives the team a connection to a major NFL audience, while his hometown background makes the relationship more meaningful to local supporters. However, it would be premature to assign a specific financial benefit to his involvement without evidence of increased ticket sales, sponsorship revenue, merchandise purchases, or other measurable results.Ultimately, the investment is both a business decision and a personal milestone for Kelce. It connects his professional success to a city that played an important role in his development and adds another dimension to his activities outside football.The central facts remain straightforward. Kelce became a minority investor in the Cleveland Guardians in May 2026, but the size and price of his stake have not been disclosed. Article Title: Aaron Donald and Andrew Whitworth bring NFL expertise to 200+ student athletes
Article Text:
Aaron Donald and Andrew Whitworth bring NFL expertise to 200+ student athletes (Image via Getty: Aaron Donald and Andrew Whitworth​)

Aaron Donald and Andrew Whitworth’s Built in the Trenches supports AD99 Foundation ’s youth mission

Built in the Trenches focuses on football fundamentals

Aaron Donald and Andrew Whitworth continue youth football mentorship

Aaron Donald NFL experience

Andrew Whitworth NFL career

Former NFL star Andrew Whitworth and current Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald joined forces in mid-2026 for the next generation of football players. They came together to create an opportunity for the young athletes to learn directly from them. Donald and Whitworth are the most accomplished linemen in the NFL.Their “Built in the Trenches O-Line/D-Line” camp gathered more than 200 student-athletes between grades 4 and 12 for a free day of football instruction, mentorship, teamwork, leadership, discipline, and character development.The Built in the Trenches camp also fits within the broader youth-focused mission of the AD99 Foundation. The AD99 Foundation was established by Aaron Donald and his wife, Erica Donald [nee Sherman], in June 2019.The nonprofit supports young people from underserved communities through educational, athletic, and arts initiatives. The foundation has thoroughly expanded its programming around athletics, mentorship, and opportunities for youth.In May 2026, the organization announced the Team Donald NIL Mentorship & College Transition Program. The program helps graduating high school athletes prepare for college athletics through NIL education, mentorship, financial education, and professional development.The Built in the Trenches O-Line/D-Line camp similarly emphasized development beyond football.The camp took place at the Los Angeles Rams practice facility and particularly focused on the fundamentals and techniques of playing the offensive and defensive lineman positions. Young athletes learned from Andrew Whitworth, Aaron Donald, among others.The young players got more than just conventional football drills. They learned about hard work, confidence, leadership, accountability, and work ethic, which define success on and off the gridiron.They got to learn all that in depth from NFL legends Aaron Donald and Andrew Whitworth, current and former NFL players, and experienced youth football coaches who offered them insights that could develop their skills beyond the gridiron.The camp’s central focus was offensive/defensive line play. This is an area of football that often attracts less attention compared to the quarterback, wide receiver, and running back positions.The duo, who played together in Los Angeles, used their extensive experience on opposite sides of the line to provide perspective on the demands of offensive and defensive football.Their combined experience made the Built in the Trenches camp a natural setting for teaching young athletes about technique, preparation, and the mental and physical demands of line play.Every camper at the mid-2026 event received lunch and a camp T-shirt, while the broader experience focused exclusively on mentorship and character development.For Aaron Donald, the exciting initiative added a crucial chapter to his post-playing career. Though he has returned to football now, at the time of this camp, he was retired and used football as a platform for youth development.Whitworth, on the other hand, has been retired for almost five years now but has stayed connected to the game through this camp. Beyond this, Whitworth works as a studio analyst for Amazon Prime Video’s Thursday Night Football and co-hosts the weekly Fitz & Whit NFL show alongside Ryan Fitzpatrick.Aaron Donald has played the defensive tackle position for the longest time. He played college football for the Pittsburgh Panthers between 2010 and 2013. He later played in the NFL for the St. Louis Rams/Los Angeles Rams since 2014.Donald built a commendable 10-year NFL career as a defensive tackle, earning three AP Defensive Player of the Year awards, eight All-Pro selections, and 10 Pro Bowl selections.He also helped the Los Angeles Rams win Super Bowl LVI. He’s still playing for them! He returned from retirement in 2026 after the Rams traded for 2025 NFL DPOY Myles Garrett from the Cleveland Browns.Whitworth established himself as one of the NFL's premier offensive tackles during a career that included two stops with the Cincinnati Bengals [2006 to 2016] and Los Angeles Rams [2017 to 2021]. Prior to the NFL, he played college football for LSU from 2001 to 2005.He is a Super Bowl LVI champion and a Walter Payton NFL Man of the Year recipient [2021] and boasts four Pro Bowl selections. Apart from these, he is a recipient of the NFLPA Alan Page Community Award [2019] and Built Ford Tough Offensive Line of the Year [2018].
Article Summary: Former NFL star Andrew Whitworth and current Los Angeles Rams defensive tackle Aaron Donald joined forces in mid-2026 for the next generation of football players. Their “Built in the Trenches O-Line/D-Line” camp gathered more than 200 student-athletes between grades 4 and 12 for a free day of football instruction, mentorship, teamwork, leadership, discipline, and character development.
