Article Title: 'Rashid Latif is Pakistani, he congratulated me': The bond Nana Patekar shared with Pakistan cricketer nicknamed 'Nana'
Article Text:
Nana Patekar

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Former Pakistan cricketer Rashid Latif paid tribute to veteran actor Nana Patekar , who passed away on Thursday, recalling how their conversations began during the Singer Trophy in Colombo in 1994 and continued for years."I used to speak with him regularly, and it continued for many days. When we were in Colombo in 1994 for the Singer Trophy, Azharuddin and Ajay Jadeja used to arrange for me to speak with him," Latif said while talking to TimesofIndia.com.Latif also recalled congratulating Patekar when he won the Best Actor award in 1998. He was in South Africa with the Pakistan team at the time and later heard from former India cricketer Ajay Jadeja how Patekar had shared the message with the Indian players."When he received the Best Actor award in 1998, I was in South Africa with the team, and I had conveyed my congratulations to him. Then when he went and met the Indian team, he told everyone about it, that is what Ajay Jadeja was telling me. He said, “Look, Rashid Latif is Pakistani, he congratulated me, but you people did not,” so yes, I continued speaking with him," Rashid added.Latif was himself nicknamed "Nana" after the actor, a connection that former Pakistan cricketer Basit Ali also recalled while paying tribute to Patekar.“Early in the morning I heard sad news. Our very dear brother, friend, and living legend is no longer in this world—Nana Patekar Sahab has passed away. What a person he was; he acted in movies exactly as he was in real life. We had nicknamed Latif as ‘Nana’, because of Nana Patekar. We first talked back in 1994, and it all started from there,” Basit said.Patekar's death came as a shock to colleagues and friends. Through his roles, the actor often portrayed the anger, helplessness and disillusionment of ordinary people.Just four days before his death, Patekar spoke about the uncertainty of life at an event in Goa. “We all have to go someday. I don't know whether I will be here tomorrow.”Patekar is survived by his wife, Neelkanti, and son, Malhar.The actor also had a connection with the Indian armed forces . During the Kargil War in 1999, he convinced Defence Minister George Fernandes to let him work with soldiers on the frontline. He spent about 60 days at different locations, including Drass, Mughal Pora and Baramulla, and was also a member of the Quick Reaction Team (QRT).Patekar received three National Film Awards for his performances in Parinda, Krantiveer and Agni Sakshi. His honours also included several Filmfare Awards, the Maharashtra State Film Award, Filmfare Awards Marathi and the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian honour.
Article Summary: Former Pakistan cricketer Rashid Latif paid tribute to veteran actor Nana Patekar. He recalled how their conversations began during the Singer Trophy in Colombo in 1994 and continued for years. Latif was himself nicknamed "Nana" after the actor.

Article Title: Vinícius Jr.’s institute gave away nearly R$8 million in 2025: How the Real Madrid star is changing future of thousands of Brazilian children
Article Text:
From the school where he once studied to more than 30 schools across Brazil, Vinícius Júnior’s institute is using football to open new educational opportunities for thousands of children.

Why Vinícius Júnior started his institute at 21

Brazil's Vinicius Junior (7) gestures ahead the World Cup round of 16 soccer match between Brazil and Norway in East Rutherford, N.J., near New York, Sunday, July 5, 2026. (AP Photo/Adam Hunger)

The Guardian

How football became a teaching tool inside Brazilian classrooms

Nearly R$8 million invested in 2025, with a major project back home

The Sócrates Award and Vinícius's fight against inequality

France Football

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

“Football is a dream, but isn’t it wonderful if we can help kids to get out of poverty by studying?” Vinícius Júnior posed that question in 2021, when he was just 21 and setting up an institute to bring football and education into Brazil’s public schools. Inspired by the work of LeBron James, Lewis Hamilton and Marcus Rashford, the Real Madrid forward began with a project close to home in São Gonçalo. Two years later, he received the Sócrates Award at the 2023 Ballon d’Or ceremony, recognising his work beyond the pitch. Five years after the institute’s founding, that ambition has grown into an initiative reaching thousands of students, with nearly R$8 million invested in its programmes in 2025 alone.Vinícius was born in São Gonçalo, a municipality in Rio de Janeiro where opportunities for children from underprivileged backgrounds can be limited. His own route into professional football began early, but making that journey work came with a cost, particularly when he started training with Flamengo at the age of 10 and faced a daily commute of around 70 kilometres that affected his education.Football ultimately opened doors for Vinícius, but his own journey also showed him how difficult it could be for children from communities like his to access opportunities beyond sport.Speaking to The Guardian in 2021, he explained the thinking behind his initiative: “My first concern was to help these young kids to achieve more via education. Football is a dream, but isn’t it wonderful if we can help kids to get out of poverty by studying?” His ambition, he said, was to create lasting change: “We need to have more doctors, lawyers, engineers coming out of the favelas. We intend to give opportunities to them.”In October 2021, Vinícius founded the Instituto Vini Jr., financing the initiative himself and starting with a project at the school he had attended as a child. He had long felt he could do more beyond football, and the institute gave him a way to put that belief into practice.“There is still a huge gap in literacy in Brazil. It’s good that we launched the app in the school where I studied because I knew how it was.”For Vinícius, the initiative especially presented a chance to turn that conviction into action. “I just thought that I could do more and I’m doing moreInspired by athletes who had used their platforms to address social inequalities beyond sport, Vinícius looked to LeBron James, Lewis Hamilton and Marcus Rashford as examples of what that commitment could look like.“I've been inspired by what LeBron James, Lewis Hamilton, and Marcus Rashford are doing. So, I began doing something for my neighbourhood first, but who knows if it can grow across Brazil,” Vinícius toldin an interview marking the institute's launch.James had established a school supporting children through education and other services, Hamilton had supported greater diversity in science and technology, while Rashford had campaigned against child food poverty. Vinícius saw examples of how athletes could use their influence and resources to tackle problems that extended far beyond their own careers.His idea was to bring that thinking into Brazilian public education, using football as a familiar starting point to help children learn and give teachers better tools to engage their students.The Instituto Vini Jr. does not operate as a conventional football academy, because its central purpose is to improve public education through teaching methods that combine technology, physical activity and the language of the sport children already understand.One of its main initiatives is BASE, a gamified educational application designed for primary-school pupils aged six to 10. The app uses football-themed exercises, interactive activities and player-inspired imagery to teach core subjects such as mathematics, Portuguese and social sciences, while its August 2026 update aligned the programme with Brazil's national curriculum standards.The institute also works directly with schools through its CT Base innovation hubs, which provide technological tools, classroom infrastructure and support for teachers adopting digital learning methods. Its Mov.A programme takes a different route, using movement and physical coordination to help children engage with their regular school subjects.These initiatives address a wider problem facing Brazilian education, where access to private schooling and the resources it can provide remains unequal. The institute works with public-school teachers to understand what their students need, then adapts its methods to local realities rather than imposing one approach across every classroom.The organisation now reports that its programmes reach more than 10,169 students across over 30 schools in five Brazilian states, building on earlier work involving approximately 4,500 students and 500 teachers. Its stated ambition is to support the UN's Sustainable Development Goal 4, which focuses on quality education, by helping make public schooling more effective and accessible by 2030.The institute's latest financial figures give a clearer picture of how much of its work goes directly into its education programmes. During 2025, it invested R$7,996,294.17, approximately US$1.59 million, while allocating 85% of its resources directly to core activities developed with partner schools, teachers and students.In a statement published on August 10, 2026, the institute explained what that allocation means for its work.“In 2025, 85% of the Instituto Vini Jr.'s resources were directly allocated to its core activities, contributing to actions developed with partner schools and reaching teachers and students through new teaching and learning methodologies and strategies.”The statement added that the figures reflected its commitment to transparent, responsible management, with most of its resources directed towards initiatives at the heart of its mission.Vagner Rocha, the institute's head of Operations, described the satisfaction of seeing those plans become real projects rather than remaining figures in a budget.“I think working with finance and seeing the numbers become reality is always very enjoyable. We think, we project how things will happen, but seeing it in practice, seeing the project actually come to life, following the entire trajectory of what was planned, is very gratifying,” Rocha said.He also explained why the work takes on greater meaning when it reaches the children themselves.“And when you see the children participating in our projects benefiting from everything that was conceived, formulated, and built with so much hard work and care, it brings more energy and gives even more purpose to the work.”One of Vinícius's most ambitious projects brings that commitment back to São Gonçalo, where the institute is rehabilitating the former Ciep 040 Porto do Rosa Intercultural Brazil-Russia public school building. The Rio de Janeiro state government approved a competitive bidding process granting the institute rights to take over the deactivated site in August 2024, after the school had remained closed for nearly a decade.The redevelopment involves a reported personal investment of approximately €3.3 million to €3.6 million from Vinícius, with plans to create a free social and cultural centre combining educational technology classrooms, sports facilities and communal spaces. The complex aims to serve more than 5,000 residents, giving the surrounding community access to opportunities that extend well beyond the classroom.The scale of that work helped Vinícius become the first and, so far, only Brazilian recipient of the Sócrates Award, whichestablished in 2022 to recognise footballers making a difference through humanitarian work and community initiatives.He received the honour at the 2023 Ballon d’Or ceremony, where he spoke about what the institute meant to him and why he wanted to keep expanding its reach.“Very happy to receive this award and to help many children in Brazil. I had little chance of getting where I have coming from where I came so it is a pleasure for me to help as many kid as I can so they can have a chance.”His work also extends to tackling racism, an issue Vinícius has confronted throughout his career as a Black Brazilian footballer playing in Europe. The institute runs an anti-racism office that provides institutional support, educational workshops and guidance on accessing pro bono legal assistance for discrimination-related cases.In 2024, Vinícius was also appointed a UNESCO Goodwill Ambassador for Education for All, becoming only the second Brazilian footballer after Pelé to receive that honour.The recognition has followed a project that began with one young footballer funding an idea in his neighbourhood and has since expanded into a network supporting thousands of children. For Vinícius, the aim remains tied to the problem he recognised as a boy in São Gonçalo: giving children access to opportunities that allow them to imagine a future beyond the circumstances into which they were born.
Article Summary: Vinícius Júnior founded the Instituto Vini Jr. in October 2021. The institute uses football as a teaching tool in Brazil's public schools. It has invested nearly R$8 million in its programmes in 2025 alone. Its main initiative is a gamified application designed for primary-school pupils.

A man standing near the players’ exit called the Cowboys’ performance “embarrassing.” Prescott turned toward him, and the interaction continued as he questioned why the man looked away after making the comment.Video of the incident showed Prescott asking a Cowboys employee to remove the man from the area. The person was first described as a stadium worker, but the Dallas Cowboys and later reports identified him as a driver working for a third-party car service.Prescott addressed the incident during his postgame press conference. He did not completely reject the criticism, but explained that the man’s reaction bothered him.“I mean, not that they’re wrong,” Prescott said.He then explained what happened when he looked toward the driver.“When he said that, I just happened to look at him, and at that point, he looked away, didn’t look, and then when I turned my head back, he said something else,” Prescott told reporters.The quarterback made it clear that he had no problem with people sharing their opinions about the team’s performance. What bothered him was the way the driver appeared to avoid facing him after making the remark.“Feel free to speak your mind. Speak it, just don’t cower away from the reaction you’re going to get,” Prescott said. “So, yeah, if you’re saying it’s embarrassing, say it’s embarrassing. If you’re saying it to me, then say it to me. Don’t go back on it.”His comments showed that he understood why people were unhappy with the result, even though he did not like how the criticism was delivered. The loss had given Dallas plenty to think about, and Prescott was also asked to explain the team’s performance on the field.Cowboys head coach Brian Schottenheimer also spoke about the exchange. He said people were free to share their opinions and described the criticism as something that could motivate the team. His response came after Dallas struggled to stop Tampa Bay and failed to turn its chances into enough points.The Buccaneers won 24-16, handing Dallas its third defeat of the season. Prescott finished with 316 passing yards, one touchdown and two interceptions, according to the official game reports.Tampa Bay also recorded its first win of the 2026 season, leaving the Cowboys with a 2-3 record.The result was disappointing for Dallas, especially because the Buccaneers had entered the game without a win. However, Prescott also made it clear that calling the loss embarrassing could take credit away from Tampa Bay’s performance.He acknowledged that Dallas had been expected to win, but pointed to the opposition’s work rather than dismissing the result as a poor showing alone. That distinction matters because the Buccaneers earned the victory on the field, while the Cowboys were left to deal with their mistakes.
Article Summary: Dallas Cowboys quarterback Dak Prescott responded after a driver called the team’s 24-16 loss to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers “embarrassing” Prescott admitted that the criticism was not entirely wrong, but he took issue with the way the man reacted after being noticed. The exchange happened at AT&T Stadium after Dallas fell to 2-3.

Article Title: Sanju Samson matches Virat Kohli’s record with whirlwind 21-ball fifty against West Indies
Article Text:
Ishan Kishan and Sanju Samson (Pic credit: BCCI)

Two reprieves, then a record-equalling fifty

Abhishek, Samson give India a flying start

NEW DELHI: Sanju Samson answered his disappointing outing in the series opener with a blistering half-century in the second T20I against West Indies in Ranchi on Friday, matching Virat Kohli ’s record for the joint-fastest fifty by an Indian against the Caribbean side in the format.Samson brought up his half-century in just 21 balls, equalling Kohli’s effort at the Wankhede Stadium in 2019. The wicketkeeper-batter’s explosive start also powered India to their highest powerplay score against West Indies in T20Is - 79/1, surpassing the previous mark of 72 without loss, recorded at Wankhede in 2019.After managing only 11 in the series opener in Lucknow, Samson made an emphatic statement at the JSCA International Stadium, taking the attack to the West Indies bowlers and giving India a flying start after captain Shreyas Iyer was asked to bat first.Samson’s innings was as aggressive as it was fortunate. He was dropped on six in the third over and received another reprieve on 42 in the sixth, at 5.4 overs. He made the West Indies pay almost immediately, reaching his fifty two balls later with back-to-back boundaries.The landmark arrived in style in the final over of the powerplay. Facing Romario Shepherd, Samson drove a full delivery neatly through extra-cover for four to complete his 21-ball half-century.He raised his bat briefly before turning his attention back to the job at hand.His assault featured six fours and three sixes, underlining the range of his strokeplay and his intent to dominate from the outset.Samson’s response was particularly significant after his modest return in Lucknow, where India had won the opening match by eight wickets. The right-hander looked determined to make an impact early and ensure the hosts maintained their momentum in the five-match series.Samson added 42 runs for the opening wicket with Abhishek Sharma, who contributed 20 off 12 balls in a partnership lasting four overs. After Abhishek’s departure, Samson continued to lead the scoring alongside Ishan Kishan, keeping the pressure on the West Indies attack.The explosive start came after West Indies captain Shai Hope opted to bowl first, expecting the wet conditions to worsen as the evening progressed. Hope also made one change to his side, bringing in Gudakesh Motie in place of Forde.India captain Iyer confirmed an unchanged playing XI and said his side would adapt to the conditions while maintaining its standards throughout the match.“We were looking to bowl first as well, will have to adapt quickly. We have talked about maintaining standards for 40 overs. We want to challenge ourselves to get better. We are going with the same team,” Iyer said at the toss.
Article Summary: Sanju Samson scores a record-equalling fifty against West Indies. India reach 79-1 in the first powerplay, surpassing previous record of 72 without loss recorded at Wankhede in 2019. Samson's half-century equalled Virat Kohli's record for the joint-fastest fifty by an Indian against the Caribbean side in the format.

Article Title: 149.5kmph thunderbolt! Mayank Yadav leaves West Indies reeling after India’s record T20I total in Ranchi
Article Text:
Mayank Yadav celebrates after taking the wicket of Shimron Hetmyer. (Pic credit: BCCI)

Mayank strikes twice in successive deliveries

149.5kmph thunderbolt knocks over Powell

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India’s batting sets up a daunting chase

NEW DELHI: India’s batting fireworks set the stage for a ferocious pace assault as Mayank Yadav unleashed his thunderbolts to leave West Indies reeling in a record chase in Ranchi on Friday.After Sanju Samson, Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma powered India to their highest-ever T20I total against West Indies, the tearaway pacer delivered a stunning opening spell, claiming three wickets inside the powerplay to put the visitors under immense pressure in their pursuit of 250 in the second match of the five-game series.Sent in to bat by West Indies skipper Shai Hope, India piled up a formidable 249/5 in 20 overs, with Samson leading the charge with a blistering 82 off 41 balls. Ishan Kishan chipped in with 43 off 22 deliveries, while Iyer smashed 40 off 18 and Tilak remained unbeaten on 44 off just 18 balls.West Indies needed a flying start to stay in the contest, but Mayank had other plans. Bowling at searing pace, he struck twice in successive deliveries in the opening over to rock the visitors early.Mayank first dismissed Kamil Pooran off the third ball, with the batter top-edging a 143kmph short delivery.Substitute fielder Ravi Bishnoi sprinted in from square leg and took an excellent catch near midwicket to complete the dismissal.The next delivery was even more intimidating. Mayank sent down a 144kmph short-of-a-length ball that jagged back sharply, beating Shimron Hetmyer’s attempted defence and crashing into the stumps. Hetmyer was bowled for a golden duck, leaving West Indies struggling at 5/2 after just four deliveries.Mayank returned to strike again in the final over of the powerplay, producing the fastest and most decisive delivery of his spell.Clocked at a stunning 149.5kmph, the thunderbolt rushed Rovman Powell as he attempted to heave the ball across the line. The delivery brushed his back pad before crashing into the off stump, sending the batter back for 24 off 13 balls.The dismissal completed Mayank’s three-wicket burst and left West Indies at 72/3 after six overs, with the pacer finishing the powerplay with figures of 3/36 from three overs.Despite Powell’s brief counterattack, the early damage had put West Indies on the back foot in a chase that demanded sustained aggression against India’s imposing total.India’s 249/5 eclipsed their previous highest T20I total against West Indies — 244/4 at Lauderhill in 2016, when they lost a last-ball thriller by one run. They had also scored 240/3 at Mumbai’s Wankhede Stadium and 209/4 in Hyderabad in 2019.Samson’s explosive innings, backed by valuable contributions from Kishan, Iyer and Tilak, gave India the platform. Mayank’s express pace then ensured the visitors faced a daunting challenge from the outset, with his 149.5kmph delivery providing the defining moment of a devastating powerplay spell.
Article Summary: Mayank Yadav takes three wickets in powerplay to put West Indies under pressure. Sanju Samson, Shreyas Iyer and Tilak Varma power India to 249/5 in 20 overs. Ishan Kishan chipped in with 43 off 22 deliveries, while Iyer smashed 40.

Article Title: Mask and Face must face same consequences: SC stays HC bail, sends Rs 3,000 crore drug case accused to jail
Article Text:
Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: “Mask must face the same consequences as the Face”, “If your masters are in jail, you will serve them better by being there, not outside” – were the caustic remarks by Supreme Court on Thursday as it send back to prison an accused who was granted bail by the Punjab and Haryana HC in a huge narcotic drug trafficking case.The case related to seizure of 5,000 tablets of tramadol from one Ashu Arora last February in Amritsar and subsequent unearthing of an inter-state illegal drug trafficking syndicate. Senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for the accused, argued that HC had granted bail six months ago putting a premium on the liberty of citizens and because of his illegal custody.A bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana asked, given the gravity of the crime, a Rs 3,000 crore illegal drug trafficking syndicate and seizure of 5,000 Tramadol tablets, can the illegal detention prior to arrest vitiate the arrest itself as has been cited by the HC?When Singh said that his client, Anuj Kumar Singh, was a mere employee of those who were allegedly running the inter-state drug trafficking network, the bench said, “You are a ‘mukhota’ (mask) which was as much involved in the crime as the face itself.”“When your masters are in jail, you can serve them better by being there with them, not outside,” the bench said while expressing serious concern over the menace of narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in the state. The senior advocate said that there was no evidence of any seizure of drugs from his client.The bench said, “In a game of football, there are 11 players but all of them do not have possession of the ball simultaneously.”The counsel said his client was not even a 12th player. Switching to cricket from football, the bench said, “He was either a cover or an extra-cover.”The bench said it would cancel the bail, ask the prosecution to complete the trial in one year and if it does not complete, then the accused can apply for regular bail. When Singh protested saying the accused had cooperated with the investigation and regularly attended trial while being on bail, the bench said, “For a Rs 3,000 crore drug trafficking case, one year in jail is nothing.”It asked the accused to surrender within two weeks and asked him to respond to the Union govt’s appeal against HC order granting bail.When Singh cited the HC’s decision to grant bail because of illegal custody prior to arrest and the premium it put on liberty, the bench said, “We also continuously ruled in favour of preserving liberty if there are other redeeming features. In your case, we do not find your cooperation in investigation or attendance of trial in the face of nature of crime and the restrictions in law to be a very relevant redeeming feature. Your arguments are most persuasive. In any other case we would have agreed with you.”
Article Summary: The case related to seizure of 5,000 tablets of tramadol from one Ashu Arora last February in Amritsar. Senior advocate Maninder Singh, appearing for the accused, argued that HC had granted bail six months ago putting a premium on liberty of citizens.

Article Title: Love over lavishness: Indriya turns Diwali into a festival of love with Aditi Rao Hydari and Siddharth
Article Text:
The festive season remains one of the most important periods for the jewellery industry, shaped by the enduring traditions of celebration, gifting and auspicious purchases.

As Indriya continues to expand its presence across India, we see this as an opportunity to build deeper emotional connections with consumers through stories that resonate with how they celebrate today. With ‘Festival of Love’, we wanted to spotlight the relationships and moments that make the festive season meaningful, while Padmika brings this sentiment to life through jewellery inspired by prosperity, blessings and new beginnings.

Together, they reflect our vision of creating jewellery that is rooted in Indian culture yet relevant for the modern consumer

A Diwali story, told in the little moments

Aaj Diwali hai ya Valentine’s Day?

This festive season, we wanted to move beyond the larger spectacle of celebration and focus on the moments of affection and connection that often unfold quietly within it.

Aditi and Siddharth brought this thought to life effortlessly. As a couple, they embody the warmth, playfulness and genuine companionship that the campaign seeks to celebrate, making the story feel authentic and relatable.

Padmika: Heritage craft through a contemporary len

Beyond the sparkle

Disclaimer: This article has been produced on behalf of Novel Jewels by Times Internet’s Spotlight team.

Every festive season, from Dhanteras and Diwali to the weddings that follow, Indians buy gold as much for tradition and sentiment as for style. And year after year, jewellery campaigns try to outdo each other with grand celebrations, sweeping visuals and big family gatherings.This year, Indriya , Aditya Birla Jewellery, has chosen a different route. Its festive campaign, Festival of Love, featuring Aditi Rao Hydari and Siddharth, sets aside the spectacle to focus on something far more familiar. The small gestures of affection that unfold between people in the middle of all the preparation.Most households will recognise the premise. Festivals bring homes alive with decorations, rituals, gifts and guests. Yet, amid the bustle, it is the simplest moments of connection that stay with us longest. For Indriya, which is steadily expanding its presence across the country, the festive season is also a chance to build a deeper bond with consumers at a time when emotion and purchase decisions go hand in hand.Sandeep Kohli, CEO, Indriya, said, “.”The campaign film follows Aditi and Siddharth as they prepare to host friends for Diwali. There is no dramatic arc. Instead, the story moves through the familiar bustle of festive preparations, punctuated by playful banter, thoughtful gestures and the easy companionship of two people entirely at home with each other. Much of the film’s charm rests on the couple’s natural chemistry, which lends it a warmth that feels lived-in rather than staged.The emotional high point arrives as the evening unfolds. A thoughtful gesture becomes the centre of attention, prompting their friends to teasingly ask, “(Is today Diwali or Valentine’s Day?)” The line lands lightly, with humour rather than sentimentality, and that is precisely its strength. In a single moment, it captures the campaign’s central idea: that love rarely announces itself, and often finds expression in the simplest, most unexpected ways.Shantiswarup Panda, Head of Marketing and Visual Merchandising, Indriya, said the intent was to look inward rather than outward. “The jewellery at the heart of the story is Padmika , Indriya’s new festive collection crafted in 22KT gold and inspired by symbols of auspiciousness. Worn by Aditi throughout the film, the collection is woven into the narrative rather than simply placed alongside it.Its defining feature is the revival of Gulabi Meenakari, a traditional pink enamel craft, enriched here with delicate blue meenakari accents. These are paired with motifs such as Goddess Lakshmi and the lotus, enduring symbols of prosperity, abundance and new beginnings. The result reinterprets familiar festive symbolism through a modern design sensibility, with necklaces, earrings, bangles and statement pieces meant to be worn through the festive season and well beyond it.In a category where festive storytelling often leans on opulence, Festival of Love makes a quiet case for restraint. By pairing a relatable narrative with a collection that honours heritage craftsmanship, Indriya positions jewellery not merely as adornment but as part of the moments and relationships that give a celebration its meaning. It is a thought worth carrying into the season: long after the diyas are put away, it is the quieter glow of love that people remember.
Article Summary: Indriya’s festive campaign, Festival of Love, features Aditi Rao Hydari and Siddharth. The jewellery at the heart of the story is Padmika, a new festive collection crafted in 22KT gold and inspired by symbols of auspiciousness.

Article Title: 'Doesn’t make sense': Dinesh Karthik on scrapping Impact Player rule before IPL 2027
Article Text:
Royal Challengers Bengaluru's batting coach and mentor Dinesh Karthik (Image: IANS)

Dinesh Karthik explains why Impact Player rule should stay for IPL 2027

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

‘Doesn’t make sense’ to scrap rule mid-cycle

The Impact Player rule has remained one of the most debated aspects of the Indian Premier League , with questions over its influence on team strategies, high-scoring contests and India's ability to develop quality all-rounders. Royal Challengers Bengaluru's batting coach and mentor Dinesh Karthik has acknowledged the rule's shortcomings but believes the IPL should retain it for the 2027 season before deciding its future.Karthik argued that removing the rule before the conclusion of the current IPL cycle would be unfair to franchises that have assembled their squads keeping the additional player in mind. While admitting that the rule has gradually lost its relevance, he stressed that any decision to discontinue it should be taken only after the completion of the ongoing cycle.Speaking to Cricbuzz , the former India wicketkeeper-batter explained why maintaining consistency in the tournament's playing conditions is crucial, even as concerns grow over the long-term impact of the rule."When it first came on (Impact Player rule), it was very good because there were high-scoring games and there were a lot of teams that were almost chasing it down. But strangely, this last season, there were not too many close games."It just felt like one team scored a lot, and another team ended up chasing it down. And if you look at how the impact player rule has impacted the IPL, it was quite positive at the start. But slowly but steadily, it started losing the charm and the reason why it was there," Karthik told Cricbuzz.He highlighted that the rule has made an impact on India not being able to produce many all-rounders. "It helped make the game more high-scoring than what it was. But it definitely decreased the chances of India as a cricketing country producing all-rounders," he said before wanting the rule to stay this season."But what I wouldn't want is it to be scrapped for this season because teams have been picked with having an impact player in mind. So it makes a lot of sense."When you pick a team, you're picking a team based on 12 players that you're going to play. Now suddenly if you make it 11, there could be a team which is obviously not as strong as a 12 but much better as an 11, and it is an unfair advantage, and it's something that they could do away with after the end of this season."But in general, I do feel it was quite good at the start, but right now it's losing the relevance and importance that it probably provided for the fans and for the players as well," he added.Karthik further stated that a rule should be brought before the start of the cycle and scrapped after the cycle ends, consolidating his claim of why he wants the rule to stay until 2027, which will also bring curtains to the three-year cycle."But I just feel that, as a rule, whatever new rule you want to bring in, you need to bring it in at the start of a cycle and do away with it at the end of a cycle if you don't want to (continue). First of all, this impact player rule was brought in in between and then to do away with it in the middle of one, I don't think makes sense. That's all I would say," he added.
Article Summary: Royal Challengers Bengaluru's batting coach and mentor Dinesh Karthik believes the IPL should retain the Impact Player rule for the 2027 season. The former India wicketkeeper-batter argued that removing the rule before the conclusion of the current IPL cycle would be unfair to franchises that have assembled their squads keeping the additional player in mind. He also highlighted that the rule has made an impact on India not being able to produce all-rounders.

Article Title: Theatre Review: Gauhar - A rich portrait of a life lived in the limelight
Article Text:
Gauhar (Drama, Musical)

Critic's rating: 3.5 stars

Cast: Girija Oak, Neena Kulkarni, Rajeev Siddhartha, Danny Sura, Gillian Pinto, Varun Narayan and Aakanksha Kadre

Director: Lillete Dubey

Duration: 2 hours

Language: English, Hindi

Should you watch it?

Watch the play on Ocotber 11, 2026 at The Royal Opera House





There is a moment in Gauhar when the glitter around Gauhar Jaan seems to fall away, and what remains is simply a woman who has lived too much, too soon. That, for me, is where Lillete Dubey’s play becomes most affecting.Based on Mahesh Dattani’s adaptation of Vikram Sampath’s My Name is Gauhar Jaan!, the play follows Gauhar from the trauma of her childhood in Azamgarh to Banaras, where she finds love, and eventually to Calcutta, where she becomes one of the most celebrated musicians of her time. It is quite a life to fit into two hours.The play does slow down at times, and if you miss the dates and place names projected in the background, the narrative can get a little difficult to follow, especially so for those unfamiliar with Gauhar Jaan’s story.Girija Oak carries much of it, and she is phenomenal. What makes her performance work is that she doesn’t play Gauhar as some larger-than-life historical figure all the time. There is the swagger, certainly. The confidence. The extravagant woman who knew she was a star. But Girija also allows us to see the hurt underneath it with the younger Gauhar’s experiences, the rape and loss of her child at 13, and the relationships that didn't survive.Live classical music is woven naturally into the narrative, with Girija moving between Hindustani, Bengali, Marathi and English. It never feels like a musical interlude inserted to remind us that Gauhar was a singer, but showcases that the music is part of who she is.Neena Kulkarni is equally impressive, playing Gauhar’s mother and later an older Gauhar. There is tremendous restraint in her portrayal. Gillian Pinto, as Atthanni, brings some welcome warmth and energy, while Rajeev Siddhartha, Danny Sura, Varun Narayan and Aakanksha Kadre add to the period world.Lillete’s direction keeps the production visually rich, with costumes and music evoking the period. What lingers, though, is Gauhar, the first Indian voice to be recorded on the gramophone in 1902. While she became a sensation and lived a life of extraordinary highs and lows, fame could not protect her from loneliness or loss. And perhaps that is what makes her story worth telling even today: behind the celebrated voice was a woman who wanted to be heard, loved and remembered.Yes, especially if you enjoy music-led theatre and stories of extraordinary women. Worth a watch
Article Summary: Girija Oak, Neena Kulkarni, Rajeev Siddhartha, Danny Sura, Gillian Pinto, Varun Narayan and Aakanksha Kadre star in Gauhar. Based on Mahesh Dattani’s adaptation of Vikram Sampath's My Name is Gauhar Jaan! The play follows Gauhar from the trauma of her childhood in Azamgarh to Banaras.

Article Title: Nigerian held with mephedrone and cocaine worth 3.5 crore in Maharashtra
Article Text:
A 41-year-old Nigerian man has been arrested by the Anti-Narcotics Cell (ANC) of the Navi Mumbai crime branch team for drug peddling, and mephedrone and cocaine collectively worth Rs 3.5 crore have been seized from his possession.

Navi Mumbai:





A 41-year-old Nigerian man has been arrested by the Anti-Narcotics Cell (ANC) of the Navi Mumbai crime branch team for drug peddling, and mephedrone and cocaine collectively worth Rs 3.5 crore have been seized from his possession.The arrested accused has been identified as Ani Ikechukwu Darlington, a tenant at Ambika building in Rohinjan village, Taloja. An FIR under the NDPS Act. Acting on a tip-off, the crime branch led by ANC senior inspector Sandeep Nigade had laid a trap near a hotel in Taloja on the Panvel-Mumbra highway on Thursday around 6.30 pm and apprehended the accused as he was found in possession of 211 grams of mephedrone worth Rs 6.6 lakh. During the house search, the police seized a contraband of mephedrone collectively worth Rs 3.5 crore.Nigade said, “The accused was previously arrested in 2019 for drugs peddling. He was in prison for seven years and he was released on bail last year. In the past five years, a total of 2,387 NDPS cases have been registered at various police stations in Navi Mumbai police commissionerate and 3,200 accused have been arrested with seizure of a total of 1,078 kg of drugs worth around Rs 150 crore.
Article Summary: A 41-year-old Nigerian man has been arrested by the Anti-Narcotics Cell (ANC) of the Navi Mumbai crime branch team for drug peddling. Article Title: A blessing: Family in Navi Mumbai marks spastic woman’s 70th birthday
Article Text:
Every year on Sept 24, they celebrate her birthday with much fanfare. The entire housing society of Maharani Building in sector 17 participated in this special event as Vimla cut her birthday cake.

Navi Mumbai:

TOI





A Vashi family recently showed how they adapted positively around a spastic family member for 70 years. Taking care of a spastic child or a person is often seen as a “cumbersome responsibility” for the family.However, for the Vashi-based Ruparel family, it is a sheer joy taking care of a 70-year-old spastic woman, Vimla Ruparel, who has been suffering from cerebral palsy since birth.However, every year on Sept 24, they celebrate her birthday with much fanfare. The entire housing society of Maharani Building in sector 17 participated in this special event as Vimla cut her birthday cake.Her younger brother, Jitendra Ruparel (68), who is a grain merchant, told: “It’s been 70 years of sheer joy looking after our sister, Vimla, who is rather alert and can communicate with us through sign language despite her severe disability. We do not consider her to be a burden, and she has a cheerful disposition.”One of the favourite pastimes of Vimla is urging her brother Jitendra Ruparel or other family members to take her to the local beauty parlour for makeup and hair colouring. “She is quite particular of the colour of her dresses, and at times chides me in her own inimitable way if she sees me wearing an old, worn-out shirt! She also enjoys watching the popular television comedy serial Tarak Mehta Ka Ooltah Chashma.She has fixed timings for having her meals, going to the toilet etc,” said her brother, who has also kept two assistants for Vimla.Her sister-in-law, Rashmi Ruparel, commented: “I have been married in this family for over five decades, and so have been with Vimla for that many years. If I somehow become late in having my lunch, she too won’t have her meal until I sit down next to her to eat. So, she has a very loving personality which we can fathom, though others may not be able to see this sort of love.”Jitendra’s sons Amit and Sagar, besides his grandson, Aarav Ruparel, are also very attached to her, and school-going Aarav often plays with her in the house by “driving” her wheelchair.“Every year we celebrate her birthday. We also celebrate Raksha Bandhan , as I have promised to keep her happy and cheerful till the very end. Vimla has proven that being a spastic is not a hurdle,” said Ruparel.
Article Summary: Vimla Ruparel, 70, has been suffering from cerebral palsy since birth. Every year on Sept 24, they celebrate her birthday with much fanfare. The entire housing society of Maharani Building in sector 17 participated in this special event.

Article Title: Central team starts two-day drought assessment in Marathwada
Article Text:
File photo : TOITOI

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar

:





A central team will fan out across drought-hit pockets of Marathwada from Friday to assess the severity of the rainfall deficit, water scarcity, crop damage and fodder availability. Its findings will help determine Maharashtra ’s case for assistance from the National Disaster Response Fund (NDRF).The inter-ministerial team, headed by Mukundan Agrawal, joint secretary in the Union agriculture ministry, reached Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar late on Thursday. The team will spend two days inspecting affected areas in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Jalna and Beed districts.The visit comes amid concerns over drinking water availability for the coming months, possible dependence on tankers, fodder shortages, migration and distress among farmers and agricultural workers.State govt flagged these concerns in a presentation to the central team in Mumbai on Thursday. Chief secretary Rajesh Agrawal highlighted the impact of deficient rainfall and the possibility of villages requiring tanker water in the months ahead.Officials also presented district-wise data on rainfall, crop damage, drinking-water sources and fodder availability, along with projections for the next seven months.The team will begin its ground inspection at 9 am Friday, covering Shendra and Nanegaon in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar district and Kingaon Wadi, Jamkhed in Badnapur taluka and Ambad in Jalna district. Officials will brief the team on rainfall, crop conditions and water availability.The team will then head to Beed and visit drought-hit areas of Gevrai taluka, including Ardhmasla and Pargaon Japti, before halting there overnight.On Saturday, the team will visit Manjarsumba, Khandala, Vaidya Kinhi, Sonegaon and areas of Patoda taluka. It will later hold a review meeting with the Beed collector before returning to Navi Mumbai via Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar.The Marathwada visit is part of a wider central assessment of Maharashtra’s drought situation. A second team is covering Ahilyanagar and Solapur, while another is inspecting Yavatmal, Washim and adjoining scarcity-hit areas of Vidarbha.
Article Summary: The team will spend two days inspecting affected areas in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, Jalna and Beed districts. Its findings will help determine Maharashtra ’s case for assistance from the National Disaster Response Fund. Visit comes amid concerns over drinking water availability for the coming months.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.

Article Title: Mumbai-Goa highway crash: 30-year-old killed, 2 cousins injured after Honda City hits gate
Article Text:
30-year-old Akshay Kadam lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle





NAVI MUMBAI: A 30-year-old man driving his Honda City car was killed and his two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured after the driver lost control over the wheels on the Mangaon-Mahad stretch of Mumbai-Goa highway after crossing Mangaon railway station and veering off the road crashed into the iron gate of an industrial unit.The fatal accident occured on Monday around 3 am, when the three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon and were returning to their respective villages in Mahad taluka.The injured complainant stated in the FIR registered at Mangaon police station that the accused car driver and his cousin had consumed liquor before going for dinner.The deceased driver was identified as Akshay Arjun Kadam, a resident of Nandgaon, Mahad taluka. Those injured are Rohit Rajendra Dhadve (24), working as safety officer at Astriel Life Science Pvt Ltd in Mahad MIDC and his cousin Roshan Dilip Dhadve (24). Both residents of Kembhurli, Mahad taluka.Maruti Andhale, senior inspector of Mangaon said, "As the complainant Rohit Dhadve has stated in the FIR that the accused Akshay Kadam drove the car after consuming liquor along with his cousin Roshan, when they had meet near the bus stop, after which they went to Mangaon for dinner, the Motor Vehicle Act section for drunk driving will be invoked.However, as the accused car driver Akshay Kadam responsible for the car crash had died in the accident, a final closure 'Abated summary' report will be submitted before the Mangaon magistrate court. "As per the FIR by the complainant Rohit Dhadve, on Sept 28 around 1 am, when he was at home, his paternal cousin Roshan spoke to him over mobile, when Roshan's maternal cousin Akshay Kadam accompanying him told Rohit that he had come from Mumbai and asked him to meet near the bus stand at Kembhurli.When Rohit met them at the spot, Roshan and Akshay were consuming liquor inside Akshay's Honda City car. Thereafter, Akshay said, "Let's go to Mangaon to have food and the three of them went in the car with Akshay at the wheels."Roshan was sitting beside Akshay and Rohit on the rear seat. They reached Mangaon around 2 am, where they ate parathas at a road side food stall and took parcel of Khima Pav.Thereafter, they drove for 3 kms towards Indapur and took a U-turn to return to their villages in Mahad.After crossing 300 metres from Mangaon railway Station, Akshay lost control over the wheels and yanking off the road on the right side, he crashed into the iron gate of Sundha Steel Traders industrial unit.Rohit sustained injuries below his left eye, left hand and left knee. Akshay got stuck between the driver's seat and the door. Roshan's left leg was injured.Hearing the loud noice of the car crash, the locals gathered, removed the three injured out of the car and summoned 108 ambulance in which they were rushed to Mangaon sub-district hospital, where Akshay was declared brought dead on arrival.
Article Summary: Akshay Arjun Kadam, 30, lost his life in a car accident after he lost control of his vehicle on the Mumbai-Goa highway. His two friends, both paternal cousin brothers accompanying him were injured. The three friends had gone for dinner at a roadside food stall in Mangaon.
